title: KV: Cache Librarian - soft-demote probe and preemptive spill orchestration
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Fragmentation and synchronous spill to disk were a recurring cause of p99 tail spikes under mixed workloads. Evicting and immediately writing many small fragments forces page splits and stalls kernels that expect contiguous runs. This PR introduces a new small subsystem, the 'Cache Librarian', and a soft-demote probe flow that reduces eviction churn and coordinates preemptive spill orchestration with the scheduler. High-level changes: 1) Soft-demote probe: instead of immediately evicting suspect entries we mark them as 'soft-demoted' which lowers their admission score and makes them first-class candidates for background coalescing or preemptive spill. Soft-demoted pages remain readable but are excluded from continuous batching hot-paths for a configurable probe window (default 30s). 2) Cooperative preemptive spill orchestrator: long-running spill work is offloaded asynchronously using a non-blocking IO path (io_uring-style) with a bounded concurrency token pool so that spill writes do not interfere with low-latency token allocation for generation requests. 3) Fragmentation-aware scoring: eviction score now combines recency, a fragmentation penalty (favoring contiguous spans), tenant weight, and a kernel-contiguity bias that prefers victims which can be coalesced without page splits. 4) Background librarian compaction: when the node is underutilized the librarian opportunistically consolidates adjacent soft-demoted ranges into larger contiguous runs to reduce future spill overhead. 5) Scheduling hooks: the runtime scheduler uses librarian hints to avoid scheduling large compaction jobs during latency-critical windows and prefers idle windows and low token-rate shards. Implementation notes: The change is primarily in core/kv/cache_librarian.{cc,h}, runtime/scheduler/eviction_policy.h, and the spill manager runtime/io_offload.cc. Care was taken to minimize lock contention by using per-shard probe queues and atomic soft-demote bitflags. Rollout plan: unit tests -> perf lab -> canary 10% (5 hours) -> 50% (24h) -> full rollout. Monitoring: new metrics soft_demote_count, soft_demote_duration_seconds (histogram), librarian_coalesce_bytes, spill_token_queue_length. Performance: microbenchmarks on perf-lab show a 7% median and 12% p99 reduction in small-reads tail latency on mixed workloads (write-heavy background with hot reads). Memory fragmentation (measured as contiguous_free_run_median) improved ~2x in steady state, and average disk write amplification from spill fell by 18%. Backwards compatibility and safety: soft-demote is a no-op toggle (off by default), and all spill orchestration has a strict fallback to the existing synchronous spill path if io offload fails. Testing: added 22 unit tests and 6 integration tests (kv_librarian_integration). Changed files: small, focused diffs; no change to public APIs. Checklist: [x] design doc linked internally (ENG-2113) [x] unit tests added [x] perf benchmarks added and recorded [x] canary plan documented [x] metrics + dashboards prepared [x] feature-flag guarded (on via runtime flag)

release_notes: Introduces Cache Librarian with a soft-demote probe and preemptive spill orchestration to reduce eviction churn and improve tail latency. Feature is behind a runtime flag and rolled out via canary. Metrics: soft_demote_count, soft_demote_duration_seconds, librarian_coalesce_bytes, spill_token_queue_length. Advisories: monitor soft_demote_duration_seconds and spill_token_queue_length during early rollout.
notes_for_backport: No public API changes. Backport to release/1.68 recommended for customers experiencing high p99 due to KV fragmentation; keep feature flag off by default in backport.
testing_summary: Unit tests cover soft-demote lifecycle, scoring, and fallback. Integration simulates high-churn workloads and io failures. Perf lab run recorded steady p99 improvement across mixed write+read scenarios. Canary logs and dashboards were observed for 48h during staged rollout with no regressions.
